newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil telecom investment put at $100 bln by 2003.
newsitem.headline: Brazil telecom investment put at $100 bln by 2003.

text.p: Brazil's Communications Minister Sergio Motta said a proposed new telecommunications law sets the stage for federal giant Telebras' sell-off and will help draw $100 billion in investment to the sector by 2003.
"This is of the highest importance," Motta told reporters after delivering a bill containing the proposed law to Brazil's Congress.
"This would allow the government the chance to begin as soon as possible the privatization of the telecommunications sector," he added.

The minister, who hand-delivered the bill to Senate President Jose Sarney and Chamber of Deputies President Luis Eduardo Magalhaes, said he communicated to both men the importance of speedily approving the bill.
Once approved, the law would authorize the government to restructure and sell off Telebras' holding company, its long-distance unit Embratel and its 27 local operating subsidiaries.

It also would set broad policy outlines for a competitive, private telecoms sector and create a regulatory watchdog under the control of the government but independent of firms operating telecoms services.
"This creates a new and autonomous telecommunications regulating body," Motta said.
The bill establishes maximum 20-year limits, renewable for a maximum OF 20 years, on operating concessions to be granted by the government.
Motta said the law would help draw some $100 billion to the sector, up from the prior estimates of $75 billion.
The government hopes to sell off the entire Telebras system, including Embratel, by the end of 1998.
